Republic of the Philippines DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT DILG-NAPOLCOM Center, EDSA comer Quezon Avenue, West Triangle, Quezon City http://www.dilg.com.ph 30 AUG 2019 OPINION NO. MAYOR CECILIA J. CARREON Municipal Mayor Municipality of Pihan Zamboanga del Norte Dear Mayor Carreon: This is in reference to your letter dated 5 April 2019 seeking this Department's opinion on whether or not the Sangguniang Bayan could be charged with dereliction of duty for its failure to take into consideration without valid justification those legislative matters duly certified urgent by the Local Chief Executive (LCE). Foremost, the LCE has the duty to address the Sanggunian at the opening of the regular session or as may be deemed necessary, to communicate to them the priority policies and programs of the LGU. Republic Act No. 7160 otherwise known as the Local Government Code of 1991 (LGC) provides: Section 444. The Chief Executive: Powers, Duties, Functions and Compensation. - (b) For efficient, effective and economical governance the purpose of which is the general welfare of the municipality and its inhabitants pursuant to Section 16 of this Code, the municipal mayor shall: (I) Exercise general supervision and control over all programs, projects, services, and activities of the municipal government, and in this connection, shall: xxx (iii) At the opening of the regular session of the sangguniang bayan for every calendar year and, as may be deemed necessary, present the program of government and propose policies and projects for the consideration of the sangguniang bayan as the genera/ welfare of the inhabitants and the needs of the municipal government may require; Page 1 of 3

Therefore, the law acknowledged the duty of the LCE to determine what will be the programs, projects or activities of the LGU, including the priority thrust of the administration. In addition, the Implementing Rules and Regulations (IRR) of the LGC also recognized the power of the LCE to determine what matters will be considered urgent, viz: ARTICLE 107. Ordinances and Resolutions. — The following rules shall govern the enactment of ordinances and resolutions: Xxx (e) Any legislative matter duly certified by the local chief executive as urgent, whether or not it is included in the calendar of business, may be presented and considered by the body at the same ? meeting without need of suspending the rules. Further, in DILG Opinion No. 27, s. 2009, this Department said: "The LGC recognizes the competence of the local chief executive to certify as urgent any ordinance or resolution to be passed by the sanggunian. However, the LGC and its IRR failed to categorically specify as to what ordinances and/or resolutions should be certified as urgent. Neither is there any fixed measure or, at the ery least, any instance or controlling condition that will give rise to the certification as urgent of any passage of' an ordinance or resolution. The authority vested upon local chief executive certifying as urgent any legislative matter is granted by law in order to allow LGUS, at the instance Qf the local chief executivee tQ respond quickly. through legislative measures, any exigency of public service. public emergency, or calamity which requires immediate attention and solution. xxx Let it be noted that in the Malonzo vs. Zamora case (G.R. No. 137718, 27 July 1999), the Court pronounced that there is nothing in the law which prohibits that the three readings of a proposed ordinance be held in just one session day. Hence, the court ruled that, unlike Congress, the three readings in the sanggunian pf a proposed measure could be done in one session since the law does not require that it be done on separate da s." (emphasis ours) In view of the foregoing justifications, this Department opines that the Sanggunian should not take for granted those matters that were certified urgent by the LCE because the latter is granted by law the powers to determin what programs, page 2 of 3

projects or activities that will be beneficial and advantageous to the LGU. Deliberate refusal of the Sanggunian to act on the proposed legislations duly certified urgent by the LCE can be a ground for dereliction of duty because the members of the Sanggunians are duty bound to take immediate action on those kinds of measures for the betterment of the LGU. This is in accordance with Section 447 of the LGC which provides: SECTION 447. Powers, Duties, Functions and Compensation. - (a) The sangguniang bayan, as the legislative body of the municipality, Shal/ enact ordinances, approve resolutions and appropriate funds for the general welfare of the municipality and its inhabitants pursuant to Sectiqn 16 of this CQde and in the proper exercise of the corporate powers of the municipality as provided for under Section of this Code, and shall: (1) Approve ordinances and pass resolutions necessary for an efficient and effective municipal government, and in this connection shall: xxx In fact, as cited above, the three readings in the Sanggunian of proposed measures could be done in one session only to facilitate the immediate deliberation and passage of said measures, as compared to regular legislative process of the Sanggunian. Lastly, if the inaction by the Sanggunian on matters certified urgent by the LCE is intentional and without valid justifiable grounds, thereby showing no consideration on the priorities of the administration, the members thereof are considered to have slumbered on their primordial duty, thus can be held administratively liable. We hope we had addressed your concerns accordingly. Thank you. Very truly yours, BY AUTHORITY OF THE SECRETARY: MARIVEL C. ACENDONCILLO, CESO 111 Undersecretary Copy furnished: PAISAL O ABUTAZIL, CESO 111 Regional Director DILG Region IX ATD Building, FS Pajares Street, San Jose District, Pagadian City, 7016, Zamboanga del Sur LIIS/3* Page 3 of 3
